compliance.seismic: tested for Zone 4 earthquake requirements to NEBS GR-63-CORE (guide Table 5)

environmental.altitude: operating 6000 ft (1830 m); storage 15000 ft (4500 m) (guide Table 5)
environmental.humidity: 10 to 90 percent noncondensing operating, 5 to 95 percent non-operating (guide Table 5)
environmental.operating-temp: 0 to 46 C (32 to 114.8 F) at sea level, 0 to 40 C up to 6000 ft (guide Table 5); recommended ambient 0 to 40 C with liquid cooling (Table 23)

features.leak-detection: leakage detection controller with the LEAKAGE lamp; the ON/OFF button restarts boot after a leak (guide, Leakage Detection)
features.optics-osfp: ORHS (OSFP with riding heat sink) transceivers, 1600G; see the Hardware Compatibility Tool (guide Table 19)
features.optics-sfp28: ports 64 and 65 take 25G and 10G SFP28 transceivers (guide Table 19)

management.console: one RJ-45 console port, shared between the CPU and the leakage detection controller board
management.oob: one RJ-45 management port, 10 M, 100 M and 1 G (guide Table 20)
management.timing-outputs: one 1 PPS and one 10 MHz port on 2x1 DIN 1.0/2.3 latching connectors. The guide says they can be inputs or outputs. It also says the switch does not currently support timing features (guide, Connect 1-PPS and 10-MHz Timing Devices)

performance.osfp-speeds: 1600G, 800G, 400G, 200G and 100G, by transceiver (guide, Interface Naming; Table 19)
performance.port-count: 64 OSFP at up to 1600 Gbps and 2 SFP28 (guide Table 2)

physical.rack-form: 2OU, Open Rack v3 (ORv3) tray; no four-post rack variant (guide Tables 2 and 6)

platform.cpu: Intel 6-core 2.8 GHz Ice Lake D, 32 GB DRAM (guide Table 2)
platform.storage: two internal 200 GB NVMe SSDs (guide Table 2)

power.power-input-dc: 46 to 56 VDC from the ORv3 busbar, 110 A (guide Table 21)
power.redundancy-note: three built-in 1600 W DC-to-DC bricks with no redundancy; a brick failure disables the optics (guide, DC-to-DC Power Bricks)

thermal.coolant-flow: 10 litres per minute, 25 to 40 PSI, coolant 7 to 45 C (guide Table 23)
thermal.cooling: 100 percent liquid-cooled; OAT PG 25 coolant through two UQDB06 plugs; no fans

orv3-liquid.description: QFX5250-64OE-L, the liquid-cooled 2OU switch for an ORv3 rack: 64 OSFP ports, two SFP28 ports, powered from the rack busbar (46 to 56 VDC, three built-in DC-to-DC bricks) and cooled by the rack's coolant through two UQDB06 plugs. No power supply and no fan module is shipped or fits (guide Tables 9 and 10).

description: Juniper QFX5250-64OE-L, a 2OU liquid-cooled 1.6T data-centre leaf and spine switch for an Open Rack v3 (ORv3) rack, running Junos OS Evolved. The port side has 64 OSFP ports (1.6 TbE, for ORHS transceivers with a riding heat sink) in two banks of eight columns of four, with a lamp for every port. It also has two SFP28 ports (10 or 25 GbE), the RJ-45 management and console ports, a USB port, the 10 MHz and 1 PPS connectors, the ON/OFF and reset buttons and the LEAKAGE, ID, SYS and ALM lamps. A switch handle stands at each end of the port bank. The rear has no power supplies and no fan modules. It carries a coolant outlet (hot) and inlet (cold) UQDB06 plug at the ends and the IT gear input connector in the middle, which blind-mates with the rack's busbar. It is the only model the guide describes.

gaps.wanted: A QFX5250 datasheet and the maker's studio photographs of the model, front and rear. None was found, so the chassis colour, the finish of the levers and handles, the lamp colours and the legends' ink are not read off hardware. The front and rear are drawn from guide figures 10 and 11 alone.

An Open Rack mount value and an ORv3 rail kit contract (the library has neither; the guide names no rail kit). The body is a 2OU tray, 21 in wide: `ru: 2` is the guide's count of Open Rack units, and a viewer that treats it as two 44.45 mm EIA units draws a tray that is 21 in wide and 96 mm tall in a 19-in rack. The sibling celestica/ds6001 states no `ru` instead.
The maximum power output. Table 21 and the power text say 4300 W; Table 9 says 4800 W. 4300 W is used.
A leader or a photograph showing which cage each of the 64 lamps serves. The lamps are numbered 0 to 63 and the number is taken as the port number; the figure draws no leader.

What the small "U" and arch marks printed beside the two SFP28 cages mean; they are not drawn. The guide's callout 11 names only the cages. The SFP28 role is "in-band management ports" in the front-panel text and network ports in Table 19.
The console jack draws no lamps in figure 10; the management jack's two lamps are described in Table 14.
The depth of the UQDB06 plugs and the busbar connector; no figure gives one.
The lamp colours of the management jack beyond "green" for link activity and "solid green" for 1 Gbps (Table 14); the speed lamp's colours at 10 and 100 Mbps are not stated.
A rating label, if any; the rear figure draws none.

liquid-cooling.description: The two UQDB06 quick-disconnect plugs, outlet (hot) and inlet (cold), that blind-mate with the rack's coolant manifolds.

mgmt.mixed: the way into the box from the port side - an RJ-45 console port, an RJ-45 management port, a USB port, the ON/OFF button and the recessed reset button. Five parts, one purpose: reaching, starting and recovering the switch when the data plane cannot.

osfp.description: 64 OSFP ports, numbered 0 to 63 down each column of four, for ORHS transceivers (OSFP with a riding heat sink).

port-leds.description: One bicolour red and green lamp per OSFP port, numbered with the port (guide Table 17).

power-input.description: The IT gear input connector that blind-mates with the ORv3 busbar.

sfp28.description: Ports 64 and 65 as printed, rel-pos carrying the printed number, since the origin token cannot express a block that starts at 64. 10 or 25 GbE; the guide calls them in-band management ports.

status-leds.description: The chassis lamps ID, SYS and ALM (guide Table 13) and LEAKAGE (Table 24).

timing.description: the 10 MHz and 1 PPS connectors, two coaxial jacks for the timing references, which the guide says can be inputs or outputs (the switch does not currently support timing features)

name: qfx5250-64oe-l

chassis.note: guide Table 4: 3.649 in (9.27 cm) high, 21 in (53.34 cm) wide, 31.71 in (80.5 cm) deep, 105.82 lb (48.00 kg). The inch figures are used (92.68, 533.4 and 805.43 mm) and the centimetre ones in the same cells are rounded copies. Table 2 says "2 OU - for liquid-cooled model". 2 OU is two Open Rack units of 48 mm, so 96 mm of pitch, of which the body fills 92.7. `ru: 2` states those two units (the guide's own count): the schema has no Open Rack `mount` value, so the unit is the ORv3 rack's and not an EIA U, and the DCIM export writes 2 for it. The body is the whole outline of the flat figures: no rack ears are drawn (the ORv3 tray carries ejector levers and handles instead).

colour.note: The figures are line drawings with no colour and no photograph is held. The chassis colour is the sampled sheet metal of juniper/qfx5130-32cd (#8a8a8b), borrowed as the Juniper data-centre switch finish, and is estimated.

cooling.note: 100 percent liquid-cooled, no fans (Table 9, "Fan modules 0"; Table 5, noise not applicable). Coolant OAT PG 25 through UQDB06 plugs; flow 10 litres a minute, 25 to 40 PSI, coolant 7 to 45 C, ambient 0 to 40 C (Table 23). The rack's manifold ports are 96 mm apart (figure 16). The chassis airflow is none; the schema has no value for it, so `chassis.airflow` is left out.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide says rails are not provided with the switch and that standard 1OU ORv3 rails must be used to install the 2OU switch (note under figure 2); it names no rail kit part number. The library has no Open Rack mount value and no ORv3 rail kit contract, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out.

gate-1.note: Figure 10 (g051820) is a 3144 x 1200 px raster in the PDF. Its outer frame measures 2699 x 468 px, an aspect of 5.767 against the table's 533.4 / 92.68 = 5.755 (0.2 percent), so it is orthographic and carries geometry. Scale 5.055 px/mm on both axes, origin the outer frame's top-left corner; every front position is read at that scale and is good to about 0.3 mm. Figure 11 (g051821, 3000 x 904 px) has an outer frame of aspect 5.80 (0.8 percent out); its scale is taken across, 5.09 px/mm, and the rear positions are good to about 0.5 mm.

handles-and-levers.note: Callout 1 (two switch handles) points at the two tall capsule recesses either side of the port banks (8.9 and 8.4 mm wide, 53 mm tall, at 52.4 and 473.5 mm); callout 2 (two ejector levers) at the grey bars along the top edge, 4.7 mm tall, from 11.5 to 240.7 mm and 290.6 to 522.3 mm, with a latch box at the join. They are decor: they are drawn as the figure draws them and estimated. The pins that stand out of the frame at each end of the lever line are not drawn.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement. None was found and the guide, published 2026-06-17, states none; the model was announced in June 2026. The device states none announced. Estimated, since a negative search is not the maker's statement.

logo.note: The maker's logo and its lockup are printed at the upper left of the face, above the model name. The logo is not drawn: a logo-zone region is reserved where it stands, and the model name is drawn as plain text. The figure prints the model as "QFX5250-64OE-L".

no-frus.note: "QFX5250-64OE-L, the liquid-cooled QFX5250 switch, does not have any FRUs" (guide, QFX5250 Field-Replaceable Units); Table 9 gives 0 slots for power supplies and 0 for fan modules, none shipped. There is no bay on either face. The three DC-to-DC 1600 W bricks the show chassis hardware output names (PSM 0 to 2, BUILTIN) are inside the chassis, built in, and not field-replaceable units, so they are part of the chassis and are recorded in the power figures and here, not as bays. The SSDs are two internal 200 GB NVMe drives reached from the underside under a cover plate and, on this model, a heatsink (guide figures 31 to 35); they are not on a face and are not modelled as a bay.

port-lamps.note: Each OSFP port has one bicolour lamp, red and green (guide Table 17). Figure 10 draws 64 small lamps in sixteen stacks of four, numbered 0 to 63 beside them: 0 to 15 left of the first four columns (four stacks, one at each row's height), 16 to 31 and 32 to 47 either side of the gap between the banks (left stack 16 to 31, right 32 to 47), and 48 to 63 right of the last column. A stack is four lamps 2.8 mm apart centred on its row, and the lamp number is the port number it serves. Stack x positions 64.3, 264.0, 269.0 and 469.4 mm; the printed numbers stand on the outer side (right of the left-edge stack, left of the right-edge stack). That the lamp number is the port number is the guide's label under the lamp matrix ("LED lane 0 to 63") read with its lamp tables; the figure does not draw a leader from a lamp to a cage.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal in the bands between the rows, each column prints "n up-arrow, down-arrow n+1" between rows one and two and "n+2 up-arrow, down-arrow n+3" between rows three and four, so column c holds ports 4c to 4c+3 from the top and the ports run 0 to 31 across the left bank and 32 to 63 across the right (guide callout 10, Table 7: 64 ports numbered 0 to 63). The two SFP28 ports print "down-arrow 64" above the upper and "up-arrow 65" below the lower (guide Table 2, callout 11). Interface names are not printed: the guide names them et-0/0/N, with N the port number as printed, so the OSFP ports are et-0/0/0 to et-0/0/63 and the SFP28 ports et-0/0/64 and et-0/0/65, all on FPC 0 and PIC 0 (Table 19); that is recorded here and not in an interfaces block, because the face does not print it.

ports.note: Figure 10: 64 OSFP openings in two banks of eight columns of four. Each opening is 23.1 mm wide on a 23.1 mm pitch (abutting, as the registry's std/osfp). The left bank starts at 71.2 mm and ends at 256.0, the right bank starts at 276.2 and ends at 461.0, so the two banks sit symmetric about the face centre (266.7) to 0.7 mm. Row centres read 19.3, 39.2, 57.5 and 77.4 mm: rows one and two are a stacked pair 19.9 apart, rows three and four another 19.9 apart, 18.3 between the pairs. The openings drawn are 12.7 mm tall; the registry's 13.5 is used. Estimated within 0.3 mm.

power.note: Table 21: DC input 46 to 56 VDC (minimum 46), 110 A, maximum power output 4300 W, maximum consumption 3435 W and typical 3375 W, both loaded with DR optics. The guide says the switch converts the 46 to 56 V of the rack to a maximum output of 4300 W; Table 9 prints 4800 W for the same figure (recorded as a gap, 4300 used, since it is the figure in three places). The rack supplies 46 to 56 V (51 V at the bricks) and the chassis states power dc, the nearest word the schema has: its dc is telecom -48 V and an ORv3 busbar is a positive rail, recorded here and in the attrs, as celestica/ds6001 does.

rear.note: Figure 11 (guide Table 8), seen from the rear, left to right: the coolant outlet (hot) plug at the left end (callout 1, "Outlet (Hot)"), the IT gear input connector in the middle (callout 2) and the coolant inlet (cold) plug at the right (callout 3, "Inlet (Cold)"). Each plug stands in a rounded housing 45 mm wide and 62 mm tall, 8.0 mm from its end, round plug 29.5 mm across at x 30.3 and 500.2, y 62.2. The IT gear connector is a 26 mm wide blind-mate clip body with a round stud plate either side (59 mm over both) and an earth mark above it. Thirteen round screw heads are spaced over the plate (decor; four small cross-head screws at the plug plates are not drawn). The plugs are the guide's UQDB06 universal quick-disconnect blind-mate plugs of the Open Compute standard, and the connector engages the busbar of the rack as the switch slides in.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5250 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-06-17, 140 pages (copyright Juniper Networks, 2026), from https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/qfx5250/qfx5250.pdf: the front and rear views (figures 8 and 9), the front panel (figure 10, Table 7) and rear panel (figure 11, Table 8) with their flat figures g051820 and g051821, Table 2 (key specifications), Table 4 (physical specifications), Table 5 (environmental), Table 6 (models), Tables 9 and 10 (power and cooling, configurations), Tables 12 to 18 (lamps and buttons), Tables 19 and 20 (ports), the Channelization list (page 48), the section "Connect 1-PPS and 10-MHz Timing Devices" (page 85), Tables 21 to 24 (power and flow), Tables 25 and 26 (packing list) and the agency approvals. It is a public document of the maker. Terms: a copyright notice and an end-user licence agreement only. No public datasheet for the QFX5250 was found (the maker's datasheet pages and a search for one turned up none), and Juniper's image library has no photograph of this model at the address its other models use (qfx-series/QFX5250-64OE-L/QFX5250-64OE-L-front-high.jpg and -rear-high.jpg both answer 404, as do the lower case and the QFX5250-64OE spellings). The Juniper community post announcing the model carries only stock and screenshot images. So no photograph, Visio stencil or 3D model was held or found, and the guide's two flat figures are the only source of the faces.

stack-orientation.note: The connector slot stands at 0.55 of the opening's height in rows one and two and at 0.41 and 0.44 in rows three and four, so the lower pair is the upper pair turned over: rows one and two are drawn 0 and rows three and four 180, each pair turned alike as the OSFP MSA stacks are (lint L108). Read off the figure's cage art, not seen on hardware.

status-and-mgmt.note: Figure 10, right of the right bank: the ON/OFF button (a grey disc, callout 5) above the 10MHz and 1PPS DIN connectors (callout 4, a pair of round coaxial jacks 6.9 mm across, 7.9 mm apart); the MGMT jack (callout 3) with a Torx screw above and below it; the LEAKAGE lamp (callout 6); the CONSOLE jack (callout 9) with the ID, SYS and ALM lamps (callout 7) beside it, the USB 3.0 Type-A port with the SuperSpeed mark (callout 8) and the RST pinhole. Both jacks stand turned a quarter turn, the latch on the right; the MGMT jack shows its two lamps at the top and bottom of the right edge (guide Table 14: link activity and status), the console jack none. The lamps ID, SYS, ALM and LEAKAGE are narrow vertical slots. At the left of the face, the two SFP28 cages are stacked (callout 11), both turned a quarter turn with the latch on the right, framed by a printed bracket; below them is the serial-number pull-tab with its QR code (callout 12).

timing-connector.note: Guide section "Connect 1-PPS and 10-MHz Timing Devices" (printed page 85, PDF page 92): the ports "require 2x1 DIN 1.0/2.3 latching plug connectors", which is the library's common/din-1-0-2-3-jack. The same section says the ports can serve as inputs or outputs, and that the switch "does not currently support timing features".

variants.note: Table 6 lists one model, QFX5250-64OE-L, for the ORv3 rack; Table 10 lists one hardware configuration with no spare-chassis part number; the regulatory model is also QFX5250-64OE-L. The guide describes no AC, DC, air cooled, four-post-rack or bays-open variant, so the device has one configuration. The table's other columns (AC PSU powered, DC PSU powered, air cooled, four-post rack) are empty for it.

placements.description: Table 24 - red steady: a leak is detected and the alarm has been triggered; unlit: normal operation, no leak
Table 13 - blue blinking: the beacon feature is enabled (request chassis beacon fpc 0 on); unlit: not enabled
Table 13 - green blinking: loading Junos OS Evolved or shutting down; green steady: Junos OS Evolved is loaded; unlit: powered off or halted
Table 13 - red steady: a major fault; yellow steady: a minor fault; red and yellow blinking: a major and a minor fault with the device halted; unlit: halted or no alarm

UQDB06 plug (inlet) - introduces the coolant into the switch (guide Table 8, callout 3)
IT gear input connector - blind-mates with the ORv3 busbar (guide Table 8, callout 2)
